title: Laufey Signs With UTA in All Areas
description: Fast-rising Grammy-winning singer-songwriter Laufey has signed with United Talent Agency for global representation in all areas, the company announc
body:
Fast-rising Grammy-winning singer-songwriter Laufey has signed with United Talent Agency for global representation in all areas, the company announced early Monday. UTA will work to secure opportunities across live touring, media, filmed entertainment, brand partnerships, and more.

	The signing comes as Laufey — whose fusion of pop and traditional jazz has introduced a decade-sold style to new generations — is in the midst of a major global tour behind her Grammy-winning 2025 album, “A Matter of Time,” playing across North America, UK, Europe, Asia, and Oceania. That album, who reached No. 4 on the Billboard 200, and her second full-length, “2023’s “Bewitched,” both won Grammy Awards for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album.
	

	The singer, of Chinese-Icelandic descent, was awarded the Knight’s Cross of the Order of the Falcon by Iceland President Halla Tómasdóttir, which is the highest national distinction for citizens who have made significant contributions to the nation’s cultural, artistic, and international reputation. She was also named one of Time magazine’s 2025 women of the year and was honored at Variety’s 2024 Hitmakers event with the Crossover Artist of the Year award.


	Despite the honors and acclaim — and the fierce jazz chops she displays on guitar — Laufey backs away from considering herself a jazz musician. “I think one of the reasons I don’t fully call myself a jazz artist is because I don’t think every single one of my songs falls directly under that category, and it could be insulting to those who do full jazz to say that it is a fully jazz album,” she told Variety. “That being said, there are lots of tracks in my discography and on ‘Bewitched that do resemble jazz standards and would be very, very at home in a jazz setting. So it’s so hard to put me under any kind of category. If I were in a pop category, I wouldn’t feel completely at home, either. So that’s kind of the only reason I haven’t claimed it.”
	

	However, she continued, “I grew up listening mostly to classical and jazz, and jazz music is where all my vocal inspiration has come from. And I’m a trained jazz singer; that’s what I studied. So (topping that chart) was such an honor. I really would’ve never believed it, and especially not with an audience as young as mine, and an audience of listeners that don’t typically listen to jazz music. I think that’s what made it so cool.”

schema.headline: Laufey Signs With UTA in All Areas

title: Imax China Prepares Full ‘Odyssey’ Rollout Across Nearly 800 Screens as CEO Cites the ‘Christopher Nolan Effect’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Imax China is preparing to dedicate the vast majority of its nearly 800-screen network to Christopher Nolan‘s “The Odyssey” when the film opens in m
body:
Imax China is preparing to dedicate the vast majority of its nearly 800-screen network to Christopher Nolan‘s “The Odyssey” when the film opens in mainland China on Aug. 14, with CEO Daniel Manwaring telling Variety that audience anticipation for the release “is going to be enormous.”

	“I’m expecting a very large majority of our entire network, if not all of our network, that first week will be playing ‘The Odyssey,'” Manwaring says.
	

	Nolan and star Matt Damon are set to arrive in Beijing on July 30 for what Manwaring describes as the first-ever red carpet event held for a commercial film at the China National Film Museum in Beijing, a government institution that also hosted the original Chinese launch of “Avatar” in Imax’s early years in the country. 


	Two screenings are planned in Beijing, alongside a separate event at an Imax theater at Universal Beijing Resort. “We haven’t seen enthusiasm for a film like this in quite some time,” says Manwaring, noting that he’s personally been receiving “50 to 60 WeChats” every day of people requesting tickets for the movie.

	Previews begin Aug. 1 and 2 in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou and Shenzhen, with one screening per day ahead of the wide release. Manwaring notes that Imax China is already “firing on all cylinders” thanks to strong pre-sales on “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” two weeks earlier, but he does distinguish between the two films’ audiences, calling “The Odyssey” “more of a first-tier city type of film” and comparing the geographic split to North America, where “the best performance of ‘Odyssey’ is most likely going to be New York, L.A., Chicago.”
	

	Imax’s early box office share in Hong Kong and Taiwan has already topped 30% in both markets, with combined receipts there approaching half a million dollars — “a lot for small, tiny, island markets,” Manwaring says.

	According to ticketing agency Maoyan Pro, cumulative “want to see” registrations for “The Odyssey” had surpassed 252,000 as of July 24, putting it ahead of every other upcoming imported title tracked by the platform. Maoyan Pro data shows early interest concentrated among users in tier-one and tier-two cities and among moderate-to-frequent moviegoers. For comparison, Maoyan Pro’s want-to-see tally for “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” stands at 810,000, versus 234,000 for “Minions & Monsters,” 203,000 for “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” 189,000 for “Toy Story 5” and 115,000 for “Backrooms.” Among local titles, “Kung Fu Soccer” leads with 649,000.

	Pre-sales for “The Odyssey” have not yet opened in mainland China, though Maoyan Pro notes that recent Hollywood imports “Minions & Monsters” and “Toy Story 5” each surpassed RMB14 million ($2.1 million) in pre-sales, with “Project Hail Mary” surpassing RMB12 million ($1.8 million). Maoyan Pro also points to “Oppenheimer” as a benchmark for Imax’s pull with Chinese audiences on visual-effects-driven titles: that film generated RMB452 million ($66.8 million) in cumulative mainland China box office, with the Imax format alone contributing RMB137 million ($20.2 million), over 30% of the total.

	Nolan’s massive popularity in China has been building over time, and he’s become “bigger than any movie star” in the country, according to Manwaring. “Nolan is so big in China, and his following is not just enormous but extremely sticky. These are fans that are lifelong… diehard,” he says. Nolan’s previous film, “Oppenheimer,” took in $9 million in China in its first five days and closed with close to $20 million for its run.

	Nolan’s profile “was a small snowball and it has just been continuously getting bigger and bigger and bigger,” Manwaring says, tracing the arc from a “Memento” re-release through “Dark Knight,” “Dark Knight Rises” and “Oppenheimer.” He calls the phenomenon “the Nolan effect, or the snowball, if you will,” and says it “has just gotten so enormous” as illustrated by the performance of “Oppenheimer.”
	

	Asked what gives him confidence “The Odyssey” can become a genuine event movie, he calls the “Christopher Nolan effect” the single biggest reason for Imax’s optimism. On the film itself, the exec says, “We’re talking about one of the greatest poems ever made and told through the greatest filmmaker’s lens ever made.”

	On the format side, Manwaring says there are still no 70mm Imax locations anywhere in Asia, though the company is in “very serious discussion” to bring the format to the region. In the meantime, China’s six mainland GT theaters – extremely powerful laser-projector setups built during Imax’s earlier “institutional” era, when the company was still installing systems in science and tech museums rather than commercial cinemas – have become de facto pilgrimage sites. Manwaring says the phenomenon took off with last year’s animated blockbuster “Ne Zha 2,” when fans flew in from across the country specifically to watch it in a GT theater, comparing the effect to planning a trip around the 70-millimeter theater at the BFI in London. “It would be silly to say we’re not interested in building out more of those across the world,” he says.

	“Chinese audiences tend to be much more technical, I would say, than even U.S. audiences,” Manwaring adds, noting that moviegoers there scrutinize screen specifications and laser projection systems far more closely than audiences elsewhere. “They just say, ‘OK, Imax big screen, that’s great.’ … I think the audience pays even more attention to that in China than they do in other parts of the world.”

	Imax China’s first-half results showed declines in both revenue and profit, which Manwaring attributes to a softer-than-expected Lunar New Year slate and a dry stretch in April and May, particularly for local-language titles. “That’s the nature of our business. Sometimes it comes in cycles,” he says. He points to a stronger second half, with “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” joined by local hit “Kung Fu Soccer” and Disney’s upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday.” 

	Manwaring says Imax’s differentiation from rival premium large-format brands increasingly rests on content rather than specs alone, citing Formula One races, concerts, esports championships and documentaries alongside the company’s “Filmed for Imax” program with local filmmakers, which began with 2020’s “The Eight Hundred.” 
	

	“We used to be in the sales side of the business, trying to talk about why it’s so great,” he says of the program’s early years. “Now I think every single Chinese filmmaker, if they are going and shooting a film that they feel deserves that Imax canvas, they aren’t thinking just about converting it or formatting it in post.” Asked whether a Chinese filmmaker might eventually shoot a film entirely on Imax film cameras, as Nolan did with “The Odyssey,” Manwaring says, “There is nothing more that I would love to do,” citing rising demand for film cameras among Hollywood directors beyond Nolan, though cost and logistics remain barriers for now.

	On expansion, Imax China has a backlog of just under 200 sites and continues prioritizing higher-tier cities over the lower-tier, mall-driven growth that characterized its pre-pandemic strategy, alongside upgrading older systems to laser. “Growth is a priority, and we do see the network growing in China,” Manwaring says. He points to alternative content as a tool for expanding the company’s addressable audience, citing survey data from NBA Finals broadcasts: “80% of the audience for that event hasn’t even been to a movie theater in five years to watch a film,” he says, adding that when those same attendees are asked afterward whether they’d return to watch a movie, “90-something %” say yes. 

	“A lot of people in the across the world forgot how great it is to go sit in a really dark movie theater and be immersed into a story,” Manwaring says. “Sometimes, you got to use some alternative content events to bring them back.”

schema.headline: Imax China Prepares Full ‘Odyssey’ Rollout Across Nearly 800 Screens as CEO Cites the ‘Christopher Nolan Effect’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85
description:
Bill Oddie, the English comedian and conservationist known for hosting wildlife programs including BBC’s “Springwatch,” has died. He was 85.

	Oddie
body:
Bill Oddie, the English comedian and conservationist known for hosting wildlife programs including BBC’s “Springwatch,” has died. He was 85.

	Oddie’s agent, David Foster, confirmed his death in a statement to BBC News on Monday, calling him “the country’s best-loved birder.”

	Foster continued: “Bill was a multi-talented celebrity — wildlife presenter, broadcaster, comedian, writer, songwriter, musician and conservationist. Yet it was never fame that he valued. Instead he encouraged us to respect and protect the environment. He taught us the wonder of it. He protested, lobbied and campaigned for it. He led the way and people of all ages and backgrounds responded to his call. And such a massive contribution to conservation will never be forgotten.”
	

	Oddie got his start on the TV comedy series “The Goodies” alongside his Cambridge classmates Tim Brooke-Taylor and Graeme Garden, which ran from 1970 to 1982. He then shifted to presenting and focused on his love of wildlife, specifically birds. He hosted a slew of successful nature programs for the BBC from the mid-80s to 2008, including “Birding With Bill Oddie,” “Bill Oddie Goes Wild,” “Springwatch,” “Autumnwatch” and more.


	Born on July 7, 1941, in Rochdale, Lancashire, England, Oddie moved to Birmingham at a young age and was raised by his father and grandmother. He went on to study English literature at Cambridge University, and it was there that he became interested in comedy, appearing in several productions of the sketch comedy troupe Footlights. 

	In the late ’60s, he began his venture into show business as a key member of the BBC radio program “I’m Sorry, I’ll Read That Again,” on which several of his musical compositions were featured. After writing and performing on comedy series including “Twice a Fortnight” and “Broaden Your Mind,” Oddie got his big break with “The Goodies,” known for its surreal sketches and situational comedy. In addition to writing and acting on the series, Oddie wrote all the music including co-penning the show’s theme song.
	

	In the mid-’80s, Oddie became increasingly interested in wildlife, drawing from his lifelong passion of birdwatching. This kickstarted the second phase of his career, in which he became a beloved nature presenter known for programs including “Oddie in Paradise” (1985), “Birding With Bill Oddie” (1997-1998, 2000), “Bill Oddie Goes Wild” (2001-2003), “Bill Oddie’s How to Watch Wildlife” (2005-2006), “Springwatch” (2005-2008), “Autumnwatch” (2006-2008) and “Bill Oddie’s Wild Side” (2008).

	In 2003, he was made an OBE for his services to wildlife conservation.

	Oddie is survived by his wife Laura and daughters Bonnie, Kate and Rosie.

schema.headline: Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85

title: Sasikumar’s ‘Vadhandhi’ Season 2 Sets August Premiere on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Prime Video will globally premiere “Vadhandhi – The Mystery of Mani” this August, the streamer revealed, bringing back its Tamil-language original s
body:
Prime Video will globally premiere “Vadhandhi – The Mystery of Mani” this August, the streamer revealed, bringing back its Tamil-language original suspense thriller franchise for a second season.

	Andrew Louis, who created and wrote the first season, returns to write and direct Season 2, with Pushkar and Gayatri overseeing the project as creative producers under their Wallwatcher Films banner. Across eight episodes, M. Sasikumar plays SI Moosa Raza, a lawman whose search for answers puts him at odds with political pressure, press attention and his own weaknesses. Yashwanth, Anagha Maruthora, Aparna Das, Vivek Prasanna, Revathy Sharma and Arjun Nandhakumar round out the cast in pivotal roles.
	

	Set in Madurai, the season weaves its investigation narrative through the culturally rich backdrop of the Jallikattu festival, continuing the franchise’s throughline of rumor versus reality. The case begins when skeletal remains surface during ceremonies marking the launch of a highway project, a discovery that puts Moosa Raza on the trail of an elusive prisoner named Mani.


	The series will stream on Prime Video in Tamil, with dubs in Telugu and Hindi and subtitles in 15 languages including English, worldwide from Aug. 7. 

	“Stories from the South have received immense love and appreciation from audiences across the world, and ‘Vadhandhi’ is a franchise we are incredibly proud of. The first season carved a unique space in the suspense crime drama genre by masterfully blurring the lines between rumor and reality, and we are thrilled to bring the second season to audiences worldwide. With Andrew Louis at the helm once again, and a gripping narrative set against the vibrant cultural landscape of Madurai, season 2 takes the franchise to new heights. It is a privilege to continue our collaboration with Pushkar and Gayatri, whose ability to craft compelling, culturally rooted stories with universal appeal is unmatched. We are confident this season will keep audiences on the edge of their seats,” said Nikhil Madhok, director and head of originals, Prime Video India.
	

	Wallwatcher Films, founded by Pushkar and Gayatri, previously produced both seasons of “Suzhal – The Vortex,” the franchise’s first season, “Vadhandhi – The Fable of Velonie,” and the series “Exam” for Prime Video, along with the short “The Mask” and the Netflix feature “Aelay.”

	“Season 2 builds on the franchise’s unique blend of suspense, truth and perception while telling a story that is both emotionally compelling and deeply engaging. Andrew Louis has yet again brought this vision to life brilliantly, crafting a gripping narrative that stays true to the spirit of the franchise while taking it in an exciting new direction. Sasikumar and the entire cast have delivered exceptional performances that add tremendous depth to the story,” said Pushkar and Gayatri, creative producers on the series.

	Prime Video is home to Tamil-language titles alongside a wider slate that includes “Mirzapur,” “The Family Man,” “Panchayat” and “Paatal Lok,” as well as global series including “The Boys” and “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power.”

schema.headline: Sasikumar’s ‘Vadhandhi’ Season 2 Sets August Premiere on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Diego Luna to Be Feted at Sarajevo Film Festival as ‘Ashes’ Screens
description:
Mexican actor, director and producer Diego Luna will be feted at the 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival, which runs Aug. 14 to 21.

	Luna will receive the
body:
Mexican actor, director and producer Diego Luna will be feted at the 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival, which runs Aug. 14 to 21.

	Luna will receive the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo in recognition of his “outstanding career and indelible contribution to cinema.”

	The festival will screen “Ashes,” his latest directorial feature, which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival, and Luna will also give a masterclass.


	Jovan Marjanović, the festival’s director, said, “A quarter of a century ago, Diego Luna won our hearts with his unforgettable performance in ‘Y tu mamá también.’ We hoped then and know now that we were witnessing the emergence of an artist who would never cease to explore and surprise, moving seamlessly from major Hollywood productions to intimate human stories that reveal the richness of Latin American culture. Through his exceptional body of work, Diego Luna has left a profound mark on contemporary cinema, and it is our great honor to present him with the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo.”
	

	Luna responded, “It’s been many years since I’ve wanted to go to Sarajevo, so many colleagues have spoken beautifully about the festival and their personal experience there. I feel honored with the recognition of my work and very excited to share ‘Ashes’ with the audience.”

	Luna first captured international attention with his breakout performance in Alfonso Cuarón’s “Y tu mamá también” (2001), a role that established him as one of Mexico’s leading actors. This led to collaborations with directors such as Steven Spielberg, David Trueba, Gus Van Sant, Harmony Korine and Agustín Díaz Yanes.
	

	Most recently, he starred in and executive-produced the Disney+ series “Andor” (2022), earning two Golden Globe nomination and two Critics’ Choice Award nominations for best actor for his work in both seasons. The series earned eight Emmy Award nominations for its first season and 14 for its second season in 2025, including outstanding drama series.

	In 2025, he starred opposite Jennifer Lopez and Tonatiuh in Bill Condon’s “Kiss of the Spider Woman” and was nominated for a Golden Globe Award for best supporting actor for his performance in Hulu’s “La Máquina” (2024), which he also produced and starred in alongside Gael García Bernal.

	Earlier credits include the Netflix series “Narcos: México” (2018), which earned him a Critics’ Choice Award nomination, “Star Wars: Rogue One” (2016), a role that introduced him to an even wider English-speaking audience, and “Bread & Circus” (2020), which won two Daytime Emmys for outstanding daytime talent in a Spanish-language program and best entertainment program in Spanish.

	As a director, Luna made his debut with the documentary “J.C. Chávez” (2007). His first narrative feature, “Abel” (2010), earned the Horizontes Latinos Award at the San Sebastián Film Festival and a Mexican Academy Award for best screenplay, which he co-wrote. He later directed “Mr. Pig” (2016), which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.

	He recently stared in Netflix’s “México 86,” on which he also serves as executive producer and will next appear in the thriller “Eleven Days” and Disney’s live-action adaption of “Tangled.”

schema.headline: Diego Luna to Be Feted at Sarajevo Film Festival as ‘Ashes’ Screens

title: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong Urge U.K. Government to Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger in Op-Ed: ‘It Threatens to Inflict Immense Harm’
description: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong have urged the U.K. government to intervene in the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros merger, sayin
body:
Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong have urged the U.K. government to intervene in the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros merger, saying it “threatens to inflict immense harm on the British public.”

	In an op-ed addressed to culture minister Lisa Nandy, the trio said her intervention could be “prove one of the most important decisions any culture secretary has taken for UK film, television and media in a generation.”
	

	They argue that the merger will result in “redundancies, cancelled productions, fewer films commissioned and fewer risks taken,” although they acknowledge that aspect of the merger is less within Nandy’s remit than the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), which is also reviewing the deal. Nandy’s is to decide whether the merger is in the public interest, to which Cumberbatch, Cumming and Wong say “It most certainly is not.” The trio point to the fact that Paramount currently owns public service broadcaster Channel 5 as well as CBS in the States: the acquisition of WBD would see CNN and CNN International also come under the same umbrella.


	“If one commercially interested owner controls access to both [the CNN and CBS news archives], they control the raw material of our historical memory,” the op-ed, published in the Guardian, states.

	“Nandy has opened the door to intervention. She must walk through it, for the sake of everyone who makes U.K. television and film – and everyone who watches it. If she does not, we will be left without the ability to protect our industry and our culture from this consolidation. We must not push the public’s interest aside; we must stand up for it and block this merger.”
	

	Nandy has already said she is “minded to intervene” in the deal, although Parliament is now in recess until Sept. 1. The culture secretary, who managed to cling on to her job in the wake of a cabinet reshuffle by incoming Prime Minister Andy Burnham, currently has a number of high-profile media matters to attend to, including the equally if not more impactful acquisition of ITV by Comcast-owned Sky as well as the BBC’s royal charter renewal. 

	Last week the European Commission approved the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, albeit with some conditions.

	In the U.S., however, it is facing opposition from numerous sources. As of Friday, Paramount agreed to postpone the merger until after an antitrust trial.

schema.headline: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong Urge U.K. Government to Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger in Op-Ed: ‘It Threatens to Inflict Immense Harm’

title: Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: ‘I Have Not Stopped Living and I Have Not Stopped Working’
description:
Carly Simon has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. 

	The 83-year-old singer-songwriter, best known for her 1972 hit “You’re So Vain,” reveale
body:
Carly Simon has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. 

	The 83-year-old singer-songwriter, best known for her 1972 hit “You’re So Vain,” revealed the news on Monday in a statement (via People). “So many people have written to me, kindly wondering about my relative silence, asking how I am and what I have been doing. The truth is, I’ve been learning how to live with Parkinson’s disease,” Simon said.


	“It has taken me some time to understand the diagnosis, to adjust to it, and to decide how much I wanted to say about it publicly,” she continued. “Parkinson’s is different for everyone, and it can be unpredictable. Some days I’m so tired I can’t get the day moving at all. On others, it gives me a little more room to move, think, work, and feel like myself.”
	

	Parkinson’s disease, a neurological disorder that effects nerve cells in the brain, does not currently have a cure. Symptoms include tremors, stiffness, difficulty balancing and slowness of movement. Simon said that she was diagnosed after her mobility continued to worsen following replacement surgeries on her knees and one hip. 

	“Eventually, there were periods when I could not walk without considerable help,” the Grammy winner wrote. “My family and I knew that something more was going on. After an extensive evaluation at the Mayo Clinic, I was diagnosed with Parkinson’s.”

	Though Simon has been affected physically, she has also struggled with “anxiety, depression, exhaustion and apathy” after her diagnosis. “That has been one of the hardest things to explain,” she said. “It is not simply sadness or laziness. It is as though the part of the brain that sends out invitations to participate in life has temporarily misplaced the guest list.”
	

	In addition to Parkinson’s, Simon also revealed that she was previously diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma, a form of skin cancer, and underwent surgery for it amid her Parkinson’s treatment. 

	“The cancer was removed, but the surgery affected my appearance and made me more self-conscious about being seen in public,” Simon said. “I have always been more critical of my appearance than anyone else could possibly imagine (check out the irony of having written ‘You’re So Vain’), and this gave my inner critic quite a lot of new material.” 

	Simon has stayed out of the spotlight in recent years, with her last public performance being in March 2018. But despite her health struggles, she assured fans that she has “not stopped living” and “not stopped working.” In fact, she has written a new album, titled “Comes in Waves,” her first full-length effort since 2008.

	“Working on the music gave shape to days that did not always have much shape. It gave me somewhere to go without having to leave the room. It reminded me that illness can change your life without becoming the whole of your life,” she wrote. “I do not consider Parkinson’s a gift or a blessing. It is neither. It is difficult, frustrating, and sometimes frightening. I am still learning how to live with it and how to accept it without feeling that I have surrendered something essential.”

	Simon concluded her statement by saying: “These days I move more slowly, I lean on others more than I once did, and I have learned to accept that every day will look a little different. But I am still very much here.”

schema.headline: Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson’s Disease Diagnosis: ‘I Have Not Stopped Living and I Have Not Stopped Working’

title: Locarno’s StepIn Focuses on ‘Power, People, Data and the Future of Film’: ‘The Counter-Algorithm Is a Human Being Who Gives a Damn’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Now in its 15th year, Locarno’s think tank StepIn will debate “Power, People, Data and the Future of Film.”

	“Last year, StepIn focused on one of t
body:
Now in its 15th year, Locarno’s think tank StepIn will debate “Power, People, Data and the Future of Film.”

	“Last year, StepIn focused on one of the defining qualities of independent cinema: the willingness to embrace risk. One of the strongest conclusions from those discussions was that playing it safe is rarely the smartest strategy,” said Marcello Paolillo, Locarno Pro, StepIn and U30 Project Manager.


	“After all, audiences fall in love with films because they’re original, surprising and emotionally truthful. Yet we are increasingly surrounded by algorithms, sophisticated data analysis, AI and systems designed to reduce uncertainty, predict outcomes and optimize decisions.” 
	

	The event will explore how power structures, human capital, politics, AI, data-driven decision-making and increasing industry consolidation are reshaping the future of independent cinema. 

	Approaching the subject from “four interconnected perspectives,” it will allow the participants to discuss the following topics: “Films vs. Formula: Algorithms, Consolidation and Creative Freedom,” “Sustainable Indie Financing: Connecting Private Investors with Sales Agents and Market Realities,” “Why Cinema Still Matters: Activism, Social Relevance and Audience Renewal” and “Gender Equality and the Cost of Inclusion: Who Can Afford to Build a Career in This Industry?”

	“For many people, algorithms have become synonymous with the death of art. At the same time, there’s another perspective. Used intelligently, data can become a valuable tool rather than a creative constraint,” noted Paolillo. The same is true of AI. 
	

	“Whether we like it or not, it’s already impacting every stage of the filmmaking process, from development and financing to marketing and distribution. Ignoring it is no longer an option. StepIn wants to create a space where these questions can be discussed openly and honestly, acknowledging both the opportunities and the risks.” 

	The out-of-the-box introduction called “Fear, Lies, and the Illusion of Control” will be delivered by analyst Stephen Follows. 

	“For a century, this industry has bought tools that promise to control the inherent uncertainty in an arts-based business. This has included the use of stars, test screenings, tracking surveys, franchises, and now algorithms,” he told Variety. 

	“My thesis is that while most of them do work to some degree, (a) they don’t work nearly well enough; and (b) the industry uses them wrong. They test what they test and they produce real numbers. Sometimes those numbers even make things marginally better – or at the very least more defensible. The trouble starts with what we do next, because we mistake a marginal edge for control.”

	He added: “Once you’ve bought a hammer, everything starts to look like a nail, and the questions the tools can answer begin to crowd out the questions that matter. I’m not saying the tools are bullshit – just that we use them wrong. They are expensive comfort, and the side effects often cost more than the edge is worth.”

	Familiar IP and sequels “do shift the odds,” he noted, but “safe choices still fail all the time, and we never book those failures as risk.” 

	“We call it franchise fatigue or bad marketing, or star casting. Fame genuinely lifts returns, but the star captures most of that uplift in salary. The insurance mostly ends up in the star’s pocket, while the film underneath has become more expensive to save.”

	Then there’s “the complete misuse and misunderstanding” of the frequently repeated line “nobody knows anything.” 

	“People quote Goldman as if it’s humility and use it as cover for not doing the work,” said Follows. 

	“Right now, there’s a booming trade in certainty. Every stage, every panel, every feed has someone selling the film industry a dream – that this tool, this model, this dataset will finally crack the code. And we are the perfect customers. A hundred years of terrible odds makes people desperate, and desperate people buy dreams.” 
	

	While the platforms “measure everything and share nothing” – “Netflix has redefined what a ‘view’ is four times and Apple has never published a single audience figure” – people ignore the algorithms that already decide what gets seen. 

	“On the big streaming services, under 6% of titles take around three-quarters of all viewing. The threat is not currently to creation but to discovery. And the one move the machine cannot make is a person with taste saying: ‘This one.’ That’s what festivals are. The counter-algorithm is a human being who gives a damn, and Locarno is full of them.”

	The opening panel will feature distributor Andrea Occhipinti (Lucky Red), mk2’s Head of Production Yasmine Talli and Doris Ruth Eikhof, professor of cultural economy & policy at the University of Glasgow.

	“What [Occhipinti] has built with Lucky Red over the past three decades speaks for itself, and the recent partnership between Lucky Red and Studiocanal makes his perspective on consolidation, independent cinema and the changing marketplace particularly timely,” noted Paolillo.

	Yasmine Talli “has first-hand insight into how ambitious auteur cinema can continue to thrive in an increasingly challenging market,” while Doris Ruth Eikhof is “one of Europe’s leading experts on diversity and inclusion in the cultural economy.” 

	“Statistics about women in film remain discouraging: women are still less likely than men to hold influential positions and be celebrated for their work,” Eikhof told Variety.

	“It’s important to keep looking at them, as they tell an important story and are powerful evidence, but just focusing on statistics creates an incentive to ‘just bring more women in.’ That’s a big mistake. We need to make sure that women can stay and succeed.”

	Too often, people tend to take a “one size fits all” approach that dismantles some barriers to women’s opportunity and inclusion but leaves other barriers in place. 

	“We need to support production companies and small businesses to create the conditions in which women of different ages, religions, races and class backgrounds, disabled women, LGBTQ+ women or women with and without caring responsibilities can all do their best work. That’s not a job for statistics. That’s a job we need to do every day, in our workplaces,” said Eikhof.
	

	The good news? 

	“It’s possible, we can do it one step at a time, not all of it costs money and it will benefit everybody, not ‘just’ women.”

	Activism and political engagement will also be discussed, as “the world around us is once again creating a sense of urgency, and filmmakers are responding to it.”

	“Many of the films that have generated the strongest public debate in recent years have done so not only because of their artistic qualities, but because of the social, political and ethical questions they raise,” noted Paolillo, mentioning the likes of “Parasite,” “The Zone of Interest,” “One Battle After Another,” “Sinners” or “The Voice of Hind Rajab.” 

	“Interestingly, this has also revived an older debate: during this year’s Berlinale, remarks by Wim Wenders, followed in Cannes by comments by Paul Laverty and Park Chan-wook, brought back a question central to the cinema culture of the 1970s: whether films are, by their very nature, political.” 

	Wenders’ comments that filmmakers should “stay out of politics” were widely disputed.

	“This is something we want to discuss within the broader question whether films are culturally and social relevant in an era shaped by social media, algorithm-driven platforms, fragmented audiences, and an overwhelming flow of images. Does cinema still matter as a cultural and social force? And what strategies can help expand and renew its audience, by finding new ways to engage people across generations?”

	Overall, Paolillo remains optimistic about the future of film.

	“I’ve been in this industry long enough to have heard people announce the death of independent cinema countless times. They’re always wrong. Every few years, a new generation of filmmakers, a new movement or a number of unexpected films remind us why cinema still matters,” he argued.

	That being said, we are now living through a period of “profound transformation.” 

	“The economic model is changing, technology is evolving at an unprecedented pace, and power within the industry is becoming more and more concentrated. We shouldn’t ignore these challenges, but neither should we fear them.”

	Paolillo added: “That’s ultimately what StepIn is about: bringing together people with very different perspectives, asking difficult questions, challenging assumptions, and collectively imagining what the next chapter of independent cinema could look like.” 
	

	“I’m genuinely curious to see where this year’s conversations will lead us.”

schema.headline: Locarno’s StepIn Focuses on ‘Power, People, Data and the Future of Film’: ‘The Counter-Algorithm Is a Human Being Who Gives a Damn’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier,’ ‘Yumi’s Cells’ Lead Prime Video India’s Slate of 100-Plus New CJ ENM Titles
description: Prime Video India and Korean powerhouse CJ ENM have signed a multi-year distribution deal that will add more than 100 Korean titles to the streamer’
body:
Prime Video India and Korean powerhouse CJ ENM have signed a multi-year distribution deal that will add more than 100 Korean titles to the streamer’s Indian lineup over the next two years.

	The agreement covers 26 new titles from CJ ENM alongside a broader slate drawn from the studio’s existing library, and extends the companies’ existing global partnership with a dedicated focus on India. New and upcoming titles under the deal will carry English subtitles and dubbing in the Hindi, Tamil and Telugu languages.
	

	The slate opens with “Yumi’s Cells” Season 3, the latest chapter of CJ ENM’s flagship franchise, which topped streaming charts in 81 countries, including the U.S., Brazil, France and the U.A.E. Also on the schedule are “Filing for Love,” which ranked No. 1 in 105 countries; breakout series “The Legend of Kitchen Soldier“; and romantic comedy “My Bias, My Boss.” The deal also folds in library titles such as “Dear X,” “Law in the City,” “Study Group,” “My Dearest Nemesis,” “Search: WWW” and the first two seasons of “Yumi’s Cells.” The lineup features talent including Kim You-Jung, Lee Jong-suk, Park Ji-hoon and Cha Woo-min, spanning drama, thriller, romance, fantasy and action genres.


	“Building on our strong global relationship with CJ ENM and the deal announced last year, we’re excited to deepen this collaboration with a sharper focus on India,” said Shilangi Mukherji, director and head, SVOD business, Prime Video India. “The popularity of Korean content has been remarkable across our Prime Video markets. Compelling narratives, diverse genres, and memorable characters that transcend borders have fueled a K-content wave that continues to gain momentum year on year. By bringing a curated slate of premium Korean titles to Prime Video, we’re doubling down on our commitment to making the most innovative and captivating stories from Korea accessible to audiences in India.”
	

	The India-focused pact builds on a run of recent moves by CJ ENM to widen its footprint in the country. The studio and Prime Video first struck a multi-year global distribution deal in May 2025 at the WAVES Bazaar market in Mumbai, which gave the streamer worldwide rights, excluding Korea and China, to CJ ENM titles including “Head Over Heels.” CJ ENM followed that in September 2025 with a separate licensing deal bringing 18 K-dramas to Amazon’s free, ad-supported MX Player service in India.

	“We are pleased to collaborate with Prime Video India to bring CJ ENM’s acclaimed K-dramas to a wider audience in one of the world’s most dynamic entertainment markets,” said Seo Jangho, executive VP of platform division at CJ ENM. “Prime Video’s unmatched reach in India, combined with its deep investment in local audiences, makes it the ideal partner to amplify our content to millions of new viewers. This partnership reflects our ongoing commitment to expanding the global reach of Korean storytelling. We look forward to connecting more deeply with Indian audiences and sharing the richness and emotional depth of K-dramas with viewers across the region.”

	Prime members will be able to stream the new titles at no additional cost.

	“At Prime Video India, we keep a keen eye on what our customers are watching and what stories resonate with them,” said Manish Menghani, director and head of content licensing, Prime Video, India. “The surge in popularity of K-content is undeniable. CJ ENM is one of the biggest entertainment studios in Korea, with an expansive library of much-loved titles such as ‘Legend of the Blue Sea,’ ‘Prison Playbook,’ ‘Mother,’ and ‘A Practical Guide to Love,’ among several others – all of which will be launching on Prime Video over the next two years. The continued success of our global content deal with CJ ENM is a testament to this growing demand. For us, this deal is not only the natural step forward, backed by customer preferences, but also a reflection of commitment to making Prime Video India the go-to destination for the best international content.”

title: Deep Com Roots Sells ‘Summer Days’ to Half the World, as ISII Group Rolls on ‘Amor de Dios’ With Belen Rueda (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Flexing its muscles as one of the biggest new kids on its film industry block, Spain’s ISII Group has gone into production on “Amor de Dios” headlin
body:
Flexing its muscles as one of the biggest new kids on its film industry block, Spain’s ISII Group has gone into production on “Amor de Dios” headlined by “The Orphanage” star Belén Rueda and produced by ISII banner label Inefable Productions. 

	The news comes as ISII Group distribution-sales house Deep Com Roots has sold “Summer Days” to half the world’s major markets and cameras have rolled on “La Cathédrale,” Inefable’s first fully English production starring “One Piece” icon Taz Skylar.
	

	As a mark of its step-up in scale, ISII Group now has four films in production in 2026 and another quartet released or awaiting release, including Spanish Western “Trinidad,” an ambitious Wild West-set Spanish family saga led by “Your Fault’s” Gabriela Andrada, Paz Vega and Karla Sofía Gascón. All ISII Group titles are sold and distributed in Spain by Deep Com Roots, a strategic partner. 


	‘Summer Days’ Closes Half the World

	“Summer Days” weighs in as a sun-drenched erotic drama with a thriller edge. 

	Headed by Maggie Civantos, star of “Locked Up,” “Money Heist” creator Alex Pina’s first international breakout, “Summer Days” has closed Latin America, bought by Brazil’s Sofa Digital, plus Germany, Austria and Switzerland (Busch Media Group) and CIS (Kinologistika). Tokyo’s Aya Pro has licensed Japan, Mumbai’s PictureWorks India, distributor of Anatomy of a Fall and Flow, has acquired rights to India, and Scene & Sound those to South Korea. 

	“Summer Days” (“Días de agosto”) begins with college students Juan (Pau Simón, “Nudes”) and Gabriela (Berta Galo, “La moderna”) escaping to his family beachside chalet for an idyllic summer. 
	

	The film is described as a romantic drama. It acquires almost immediately, however, an erotic charge, in dialog and the arrival of Juan’s father Fernando (Roberto Álamo, “Riot Police”) with his much younger girlfriend Monica (Civantos). Juan and Monica’s feelings for each other build, mixing Juan’s resentment for his father leaving his mother and impossible-to-ignore physical attraction.  

	“Deep Com Roots attended Cannes Market for the first time and was met with strong interest from the international market. Among our slate, Summer Days was one of the films that attracted the most attention from the buyers,” Emir Duzel, Deep Com Roots head of international sales, told Variety. “We believe its powerful story and the strong sense of tension made the film especially appealing. We are currently continuing negotiations for distribution deals for several more territories.”     

	Early fruit of the ISII Group’s new talent support, “Summer Days” is based on a screenplay by David Sueiro, which was one of the seven fiction winners in the ISII Group’s first Break on Time ’59 national screenplay competition in 2024. It also marks a return to fiction of versatile director Chema del Prado, behind “IsiDisi,” a Spanish gross-out classic.



	

					Maggie Civantos in ‘Summer Days’
	



	‘Amor de Dios,’ Led Belén Rueda, Goes Into Production        

	Also the female lead in Alejandro Amenábar’s Academy Award winner “The Sea Inside” and star of upscale genre hits “Julia’s Eyes” and “The Body,” in “Amor de Dios,” Rueda plays Sara Lanes, a renowned dancer and choreographer now living in Paris. When flamenco school Amor de Dios, once rated the world’s best, announces its closure, Sara returns to Madrid with disciple Ángela hoping to save the place where her own career began. 

	“At the School, Sara reencounters a past she has never been able to leave behind. That and her own physical decline turns her return into a profoundly personal journey where she has to decide what she is willing to sacrifice in order to preserve her legacy,” says the synopsis.

	Inspired in its origins by an original idea by Spanish cinema great Carlos Saura, “Amor de Dios” is also produced by Inefable Productions
	

	Key cast also takes in Asier Etxeandia, co-star of Pedro Almodóvar’s “Pain and Glory,” and celebrated French dancer Soleila Chaou, Spanish National Ballet principal dancer Irene Tena and Tania Santana (“Love on a Tightrope”). 

	Scheduled for release in 2027, “Amor de Dios” marks the awaited fiction feature debut of Paula Palacios, winner of the IDA Netflix 2022 Global Emerging Filmmaker Award and a double Goya best doc feature nominee for two stirring and affecting films, set against the context of African immigration to Europe: “Drowning Letters” (“Cartas Mojadas,” 2020) and “My Brother Ali,” (2024). 

	“La Cathédrale,” Headlined by Will Keen and Taz Skylar

	“A new push for ISII Group’s fiction division,” it has noted, “La Cathédrale,” a double redemption thriller, turns on Thomas (Keen), a renowned violinist, who struggles to rebuild his life after the murder of his teenage daughter. When he agrees to take part in a restorative justice process with the man convicted of her killing (Skylar), the discovery of a mysterious violin among her belongings sets him on what the synopsis calls “a relentless search for the truth.”

	Beyond Slylar, “La Cathédrale” stars Keen, the distinguished British theatre actor and Private Secretary Michael Adeane in “The Crown,” Venice Horizons best actress Award winner Marta Nieto (“Mother”), Ronald Guttman, whose prolific and long career takes in “The Hunt for Red October,” “Lost” and “Mad Men”; and Catalan actor-pianist Peter Vives (“The Time in Between”).

	The film stands out for its “narrative tension, a powerful soundtrack and an immersive atmosphere,” Deep Com Roots has said.

	Now shooting in the Canary Islands, in Tenerife and Las Palmas, ““La Cathédrale” reflects director Eduardo Cubillo’s fascination with restorative justice. “Two people who seem irreconcilable – filled with hatred and countless grievances – can, through a simple conversation – which may or may not be difficult – end up feeling liberated in a way that has to be seen to be believed; it’s truly magical,” he has said. The film is written by Cubillo and scribe-helmer José Ortuño (“The Extraordinary Tale”).



	

					Taz Skylar in ‘La Cathédrale’
	



	Deep Com Roots’ Slate
	

	“At ISII Group, we conceive each project not only from its creative ambition, but also the commercial career it can have inside and outside Spain,” said ISII Group President Silvia Carvalho. 

	“So we have developed a structure which integrates development, financing, production, services, distribution and sales, with Deep Com Roots as the sales agent on all of our catalog,” she added. “‘Summer Days’ pre-sales and the interest generated by ‘La Cathédrale,’ ‘Amor de Dios’ and ‘Trinidad’ confirm that this model allows us to create value and market opportunities from the first stages of every film.”

	“Trinidad,” directed by  Laura Alvea and José Ortuño, bows Nov. 2026.

	Gleaning great reviews, beginning in 1969 when Spain was still under the dictatorship of Francisco Franco, “Tal vez” charts the perhaps requited love of Canary Islands poet Natalia Sosa Ayala (“Hierro”) for trapeze artist Pinito del Oro (Adriana Ugarte, “Juileta”), star of New York’s Ringling Brothers. Bowed July 10, it is directed by Arima León, turning on their encounter and their correspondence afterwards.  

	Winner of the 2025 Break on Time competition, “Desde Arriba,” a father-son relationship dramedy, is now in post-production. Martín Cuervo directs from a screenplay by Arturo Ruiz Serrano and José Manuel Carrasco.

	A realist survival thriller starring Milena Smit (“Parallel Mothers”) and Irene Escolar (“Tell Me Who I Am”) “My Zone” shot in the Canary Islands of Gran Canaria and Fuerteventura from May. It marks the feature debut of best short fiction Goya winner Cristián Beteta (“Ángulo muerto”).  Directed by Violeta Salama (“Alegría”), “Auri,” starring Cristina Marcos (“Maravillas,” “Locked Up”), a comedy turning on a housewife’s later life revolution, bowed in April in Spain.



	

					‘Trinidad’ (L-R) Gabriela Andrada, Paz Vega and Karla Sofía Gascón
									Gabriela Andrada, Paz Vega and Karla Sofía Gascón in ‘Trinidad’.  Courtesy of Deep Com Roots

title: Carly Simon Reveals Parkinson's Disease, Cancer Diagnoses
description:
Carly Simon
                          I Have Parkinson's and Skin Cancer
body:
Carly Simon
                          I Have Parkinson's and Skin Cancer
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 27, 2026
                            6:38 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Carly Simon is battling health issues on multiple fronts ... revealing she has been diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease and skin cancer.
      
    
            The "You're So Vain" singer announced the news over the weekend ... saying that along with her Parkinson's diagnosis and treatment, she underwent surgery for basal cell carcinoma, according to multiple reports.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The 83-year-old says she broke her silence because she has been inundated with fans asking if she is OK after leaving the public eye for several years.
      
    
            Still, Carly says ... "But I have not stopped living, and I have not stopped working."
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            It makes sense fans would be concerned ... Carly's last public performance was in 2019 ... at the 31st Annual Tibet House US Benefit Concert & Gala at Carnegie Hall.
      
    
            Carly's now preparing to release "Comes in Waves," her first full-length album since 2008.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Talking about her pain, exhaustion, and the mental toll of her health struggles, the singer closed out her announcement on an upbeat note, saying ... "These days I move more slowly, I lean on others more than I once did, and I have learned to accept that every day will look a little different."
      
    
            She adds ... "But I am still very much here."

title: Usher Stops Steamy Onstage Encounter With Fan at Nashville Show, Woman Responds

                          Steamy Serenade Gets an Ice-Cold Reaction

                              July 26, 2026

                                                                      |

                                  July 27, 2026
                                6:43 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Usher's steamy serenade hit a cold note in Nashville ... prompting the R&B superstar to pull the plug after a woman onstage appeared less than thrilled by his up-close moves.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            Video from Saturday night's show captures a shirtless Usher leaning over the seated fan and trying to turn up the heat -- but her reserved reaction quickly catches his attention.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Moments later, he backs off and tells the crowd, "I don't think she wanna be onstage, y'all," bringing the intimate encounter to an abrupt end.
      

            The awkward moment quickly made the rounds online, where viewers roasted the woman for seemingly fumbling a fantasy plenty would happily trade places to experience.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The woman -- identified as Gabrielle Cheyenne -- eventually fired back ... insisting "NOBODY" declined to go onstage and pointing out she had no problem letting thousands of people see her looking good on the venue's jumbotrons.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Gabrielle explained she and her mom originally had floor seats before Usher's team approached them and upgraded them to VIP ... adding she wasn’t told which performer she'd be joining onstage -- Usher is currently touring with Chris Brown.
      
    
            She also mocked critics who apparently expected her to get much more physical with Usher in front of the entire arena.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            In a separate post, Gabrielle argued her attitude only turns "nasty" when she's provoked ... saying she's quiet in real life but won't let strangers bully her over an experience they didn't get.
      
    
            So, no, Gabrielle says she wasn't rejecting the spotlight -- she just wasn't ready to give Usher the reaction his fans wanted.

title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs: Life Inside Solitary Confinement After Prison Fight
description:
Sean 'Diddy' Combs
                          My Life Inside 'The Hole' After Prison Fight
body:
Sean 'Diddy' Combs
                          My Life Inside 'The Hole' After Prison Fight
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 27, 2026
                            6:56 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sean "Diddy" Combs is doing time in solitary confinement after getting into a violent prison brawl ... and his new surroundings come with new rules and restrictions.
      
    
            We got our hands on the Admission and Orientation Inmate Handbook for FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey, where Diddy is locked up, and it lays out life inside "Disciplinary Segregation" ... otherwise known as "the hole."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to the handbook ... Diddy will be denied certain privileges for breaking the Bureau of Prisons' rules and regulations by getting into a fight with another inmate last week. Diddy's personal property also might be taken away by prison officials.
      

            While he's in the Special Housing Unit, better known as solitary confinement, Diddy will be given blankets, a mattress, a pillow, toilet paper, and shaving equipment.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Diddy is also allowed to have reading material -- both legal and non-legal -- as well as religious books.
      
    
            And, get this ... Diddy will have a staff doctor pay him a daily visit while in the "hole," which includes weekends and holidays.
      
    
            As for visitation from loved ones ... Diddy will get one social visit per week in the visiting room if he still qualifies for the privilege. He will also receive a regular briefing on his housing status. 
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            More importantly, Diddy will be made aware of his rights and responsibilities regarding the types of disciplinary action he could potentially face as a result of his prison fight.
      
    
            He will also be given a rundown of prohibited acts, plus a disciplinary severity scale that lists possible sanctions by the seriousness of each infraction, which could result in the removal of good conduct time.
      
    
            No word how long Diddy will be doing hard time in "the hole" ... but he's got some adjustments to make.

title: Wild Video Shows Food Vendor Duck For Cover During Mass Shooting at Seattle Festival
description:
Seattle Food Festival Shooting
                          Food Vendor Runs For Cover ...
body:
Seattle Food Festival Shooting
                          Food Vendor Runs For Cover ...
                          'Get The Register And Tips'!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 27, 2026
                            5:33 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  July 27, 2026
                                6:18 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A food vendor was captured on video running to safety after shots rang out at a Seattle food festival, claiming the lives of three people and leaving four others injured, including a 2-year-old child, according to police.
      
    
            Cops say the bullets started flying Sunday night at the Bite of Seattle, a 3-day annual food festival held at the Seattle Center just a block away from the famous Space Needle.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            In the video posted to X, the vendor kicks things off by giving his pitch to people to come buy his Hawaiian honeycomb treats, but before long, you can hear gunshots in the background followed by terrified people ducking for cover.
      

            One of those people is the vendor himself, who orders his worker to take the tips and cash register before they run away.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Police said two people died at the scene -- a 19-year-old and a 44-year-old -- and four others were rushed to a local hospital, where a 56-year-old woman was later pronounced dead. All of the surviving victims were listed in stable condition.
      
    
            At a press briefing late Sunday, Seattle Police Assistant Chief Tyrone Davis told reporters that one suspect was in custody, and a second gunman was still being sought, adding that two firearms were recovered.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Police believe two people were shooting at each other, but Davis did not provide a motive and said the investigation is ongoing, and there's no "outstanding threat to the community."
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson issued a statement, calling the shooting "an act of horrific violence," and thanked first responders for their quick action at the scene.
      
    
            Story developing

title: 'Top Chef' Eric Adjepong Allegedly Violated Ex-Wife's Restraining Order Before Daughter's Protective Order
description:
'Top Chef' Star Eric Adjepong
                          Allegedly Violated Ex's Protective Order ...
body:
'Top Chef' Star Eric Adjepong
                          Allegedly Violated Ex's Protective Order ...
                          Before Daughter Obtained Order Against Him
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 27, 2026
                            1:00 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  July 27, 2026
                                6:28 AM PDT
                                    
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            "Top Chef" star Eric Adjepong allegedly violated a restraining order against his ex-wife, Janell Mack, more than a year before his daughter obtained a protective order against him ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... Janell took Eric to court in January 2025 and successfully obtained a temporary protective order that barred him from contacting her by "any means."
      
    
            Well, one day after the order was set -- on Jan. 23 -- Eric allegedly asked his former wife via the "OurFamilyWizard" parenting app to FaceTime him.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A court summons was issued ... and Eric was reminded to never contact her again. The protective order was effective through Feb. 4, 2025.
      

            Eric told TMZ via his attorney ... "The alleged violation entailed Mr. Adjepong contacting his ex-wife regarding their daughter through the OurFamilyWizard app, a court-mandated communications app used during the parties' divorce and custody proceedings. The alleged violation was dismissed because the court recognized that the required method of communication was the OurFamilyWizard app, creating a conflict with the protective order."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Eric also posted this statement on Instagram ... "The past several weeks have been among the most difficult of my life. I have remained silent not because I lacked a response, but because I believe integrity is measured by how you conduct yourself when your character is being questioned. Others can choose rhetoric. I will choose truth."
      
    
            It's unclear what Eric allegedly did that enabled Janell to get a protective order in the first place. The pair were married between 2017 and 2021, and share a 7-year-old daughter named Lennox.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            We broke the story ... on Wednesday, Lennox successfully obtained a year-long protective order after Eric was accused of sexually abusing her. The allegations were brought to Child and Family Services on May 1, which then notified Washington, D.C. police, who found no probable cause that a crime occurred.
      
    
            However, a Howard County, Maryland judge issued a final protective order against Eric on July 10 ... which will last 1 year.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Food Network personality told TMZ through his attorney he is abiding by the order, adding ... "It is my fervent hope that in the future my ex-wife and I can resolve these matters privately and through the proper legal channels, rather than in the press, if only for the well-being of our daughter."
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Instagram Media.
      
    
            Meanwhile, Janell posted a statement about the situation on Instagram, saying ... "My daughter was just granted a protective order against her father because she was brave enough to speak up against who should have been one of the most trusted adults in her life."

schema.headline: 'Top Chef' Eric Adjepong Allegedly Violated Ex-Wife's Restraining Order Before Daughter's Protective Order
